events.title: US ISM Manufacturing PMI for October
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing has been hovering near expansion, and a weak print would reinforce the two-speed US economy narrative on the eve of the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus is 54.5-54.7; any drop below 54 would signal broadening slowdown.

events.title: Apple FQ4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Apple is the largest S&P 500 component and its first report under new CEO John Ternus will be a key test of tech leadership after the recent AI-driven selloff.
events.what_to_watch: Revenue consensus ~$113.3bn, EPS ~$1.98; iPhone demand and memory-cost commentary will drive the tape.

events.title: Palantir Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Palantir is a high-beta AI proxy and its results will indicate whether enterprise AI demand is holding up after last quarter's 93% revenue surge.
events.what_to_watch: Revenue consensus ~$2.18bn; guidance for government and commercial AI bookings.

events.title: Nongshim US unit files tariff refund lawsuit
events.why_it_matters: The first major corporate lawsuit seeking IEEPA tariff refunds could open the floodgates for thousands of importers and pressure CBP's refund process.
events.what_to_watch: Whether other consumer and industrial companies follow with similar suits.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.why_it_matters: All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are contested, with prediction markets pricing a Democratic House; the outcome will determine the legislative path for taxes, tariffs, and regulation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Democrats sweep both chambers or Republicans hold the Senate; a delayed or contested result is the key tail risk.

events.title: RBA November rate decision
events.why_it_matters: The RBA is expected to hike 25bp to 4.85%, its fifth increase of 2026, reinforcing the global hawkish tilt and supporting AUD.
events.what_to_watch: Any pause signal in the statement; Deutsche Bank is the lone forecaster expecting a hold.

events.title: AMD Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AMD is a key AI-chip bellwether and its results will test whether the AI capex cycle can justify premium valuations after the recent tech selloff.
events.what_to_watch: Revenue consensus ~$13.1bn, EPS ~$1.95; MI-series GPU guidance and data-center share gains versus Nvidia.

events.title: US JOLTS job openings for September
events.why_it_matters: JOLTS is a key gauge of labour-market tightness and will inform the Fed's December decision after the October FOMC showed two hawkish dissents.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~7.13 million openings versus 7.08 million prior.

events.title: McDonald's Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: McDonald's is a global consumer bellwether and its results will show whether low-income consumers are pulling back amid persistent inflation.
events.what_to_watch: US same-store sales and commentary on traffic versus pricing.

events.title: US ADP private employment for October
events.why_it_matters: ADP is a preview for Friday's nonfarm payrolls and will be scrutinised for evidence that hiring is slowing after September's weak 29k print.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~70k private jobs versus 90k prior.

events.title: Bank of England November rate decision
events.why_it_matters: The BoE is expected to hike 25bp to 4.00%, its first increase since August 2023, as energy-driven inflation forces its hand.
events.what_to_watch: The vote split and whether Bailey signals a pause after this hike.

events.title: Qualcomm FQ4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Qualcomm gives a read on smartphone and auto-chip demand, both of which are facing headwinds from memory-cost inflation and weak handset sales.
events.what_to_watch: Revenue consensus ~$10.1bn; handset versus automotive segment growth.

events.title: US nonfarm payrolls for October
events.why_it_matters: The jobs report is the single most important data point before the December FOMC, with the Fed signalling further hikes if inflation stays hot.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~55k-65k payrolls, unemployment 4.2%; any upside surprise would harden December hike odds.

events.title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment preliminary November
events.why_it_matters: Sentiment is at or near record lows, reflecting cost-of-living pressures that are a central theme of the midterm election.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~47.5 versus 48.0 prior; inflation expectations sub-index.

events.title: China CPI for October
events.why_it_matters: China's CPI remains near zero, and a weak print would reinforce deflation fears and pressure Beijing for more stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus around 0.9% y/y; any upside surprise from food or energy.

events.title: China trade data for October
events.why_it_matters: Trade data will show whether export momentum is holding up after the US tariff reset and China's own export controls on AI and chip technology.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth versus consensus; shipments to the US and EU.

events.title: US CPI for October
events.why_it_matters: CPI is the last major inflation reading before the December FOMC and will determine whether the Fed follows through on the hike priced by markets.
events.what_to_watch: Headline consensus ~3.7% y/y; core services ex-housing is the Fed's focus.

events.title: US PPI for October
events.why_it_matters: PPI provides an early read on pipeline inflation and margin pressure after September's upside surprise.
events.what_to_watch: Whether goods disinflation offsets services inflation.

events.title: Japan Q3 GDP first preliminary estimate
events.why_it_matters: A weak GDP print would complicate the BoJ's plan to hike in December and could trigger yen volatility.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~+1.5% annualised; private consumption and capex.

events.title: Anthropic IPO roadshow and pricing
events.why_it_matters: Anthropic's IPO could be the largest in history at a $1.5-2tn valuation, and its reception will be a landmark test for AI sentiment and the broader IPO market.
events.what_to_watch: Roadshow demand, final valuation range, and whether the listing prices above or below the initial $2tn target.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine-US trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi
events.why_it_matters: The talks could produce a ceasefire framework, which would be bearish for European gas and oil risk premia, but Ukraine opposes sanctions relief before a leaders' summit.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a demilitarised-zone or gas-supply deal is tabled; any US sanctions easing on Russia.

events.title: Brigham and Women's nurses open-ended strike
events.why_it_matters: The strike highlights persistent labour-cost pressure in healthcare and could disrupt operations at a major Boston hospital.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a last-minute contract deal is reached; any spillover to other hospital systems.

events.title: SEMICON Europa 2026
events.why_it_matters: The conference will spotlight Europe's semiconductor strategy, advanced packaging, and fab-management trends amid the AI boom.
events.what_to_watch: Any EU Chips Act funding announcements or capex guidance from equipment makers.

events.title: IG Metall warning strikes in Germany
events.why_it_matters: Warning strikes by 3.7 million metalworkers threaten German auto and machinery output, adding to the sector's deepening crisis.
events.what_to_watch: Whether strikes escalate into full walkouts and whether a wage deal is reached in the third round.

events.title: US existing home sales for October
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the most rate-sensitive sector and a weak print would confirm the drag from elevated mortgage rates.
events.what_to_watch: Annualised rate versus 3.99 million prior.

events.title: US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement
events.why_it_matters: The refunding statement will signal whether Treasury is increasing coupon auction sizes, which could pressure long-end yields.
events.what_to_watch: Any change to auction-size guidance; JPMorgan expects unchanged sizes.

events.title: FDA PDUFA: ivonescimab for NSCLC
events.why_it_matters: If approved, ivonescimab would be the first PD-1xVEGF bispecific in the US, a potential blockbuster for Summit/Akeso and a competitive threat to Merck.
events.what_to_watch: Approval decision and label breadth.

events.title: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs
events.why_it_matters: The 6-3 ruling invalidated the legal basis for Trump's broadest tariffs, forcing a chaotic reset of US trade policy and opening refund claims for importers.
events.what_to_watch: The refund process and whether the administration finds another legal vehicle for tariffs.

events.title: Trump imposes new 15% global tariff under Section 122
events.why_it_matters: Within days of the Supreme Court loss, the administration re-imposed a universal tariff at 15%, keeping trade costs elevated and uncertainty high for importers.
events.what_to_watch: Legal challenges to Section 122 and the tariff's 150-day expiration window.

events.title: China Fifth Plenum concludes without major stimulus
events.why_it_matters: The plenum focused on party governance rather than a large consumption or property stimulus, disappointing cyclical bulls expecting a demand boost.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the December Central Economic Work Conference delivers more support.

events.title: US Q3 GDP advance estimate 3.4%
events.why_it_matters: Growth accelerated well above the 3.1% consensus, reinforcing the soft-landing narrative and reducing near-term recession odds.
events.what_to_watch: Revisions in the second estimate and the composition of growth.

events.title: US September PCE inflation 3.6% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Headline PCE accelerated to 3.6% and core matched expectations, keeping inflation uncomfortably above target and a December hike live.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE trend and whether goods or services are driving the upside.

events.title: FOMC holds rates at 3.75%-4.00%, two dissents for a hike
events.why_it_matters: The Fed paused as widely expected, but two dissents preferring a 25bp hike signal the committee is not done tightening, keeping rate volatility elevated.
events.what_to_watch: Fed speakers between now and December; market pricing currently favours a December hike.

events.title: ECB holds rates unchanged at 2.50% deposit rate
events.why_it_matters: The ECB paused amid weak growth and elevated energy-driven inflation, leaving the euro and European bonds data-dependent.
events.what_to_watch: December hike expectations after Kazimir's hawkish comments.

events.title: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, signals December hike
events.why_it_matters: The BoJ held as expected but Governor Ueda all but locked in a December hike, keeping yen volatility elevated.
events.what_to_watch: December meeting outcome and the neutral-rate debate.

events.title: France riots calm after worst unrest in years
events.why_it_matters: The violence has subsided but the political damage weakens the French government and reinforces ECB caution.
events.what_to_watch: Whether unrest reignites around budget negotiations.

events.title: Teck Highland Valley copper strike cuts supply
events.why_it_matters: A strike at a major Canadian copper mine is tightening concentrate supply, adding upside pressure to copper prices already supported by electrification demand.
events.what_to_watch: Duration of the strike and whether other mines face similar labour actions.

events.title: Iran/Hormuz tensions; Brent above $115
events.why_it_matters: Reports of possible new US strikes on Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz are keeping a large geopolitical risk premium in oil.
events.what_to_watch: Qatar-brokered talks on a two-day Hormuz reopening plan; any US military action.

events.title: US sanctions relief for Russia via diesel deal
events.why_it_matters: Washington is selectively easing sanctions to allow Russian diesel imports, a potential bearish supply signal for oil products but a geopolitical gamble that could unsettle allies.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the diesel deal expands into broader sanctions relief ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.

events.title: China restricts AI and chip-design technology exports
events.why_it_matters: Beijing added 23 AI technologies to its export-control list and imposed registration on outbound frontier models and chip IP, escalating tech fragmentation.
events.what_to_watch: Retaliation from the US and Taiwan and the impact on global AI supply chains.

events.title: Taiwan tightens AI chip and server export controls to China
events.why_it_matters: Taipei criminalised unauthorised AI chip and server exports to China, aligning with US restrictions and adding compliance risk across the semiconductor supply chain.
events.what_to_watch: Enforcement actions and any impact on TSMC's China revenue.

events.title: OPEC+ November 1 meeting decides to maintain December production
events.why_it_matters: The seven OPEC+ countries kept December quotas unchanged, as expected, but the decision comes with Brent above $110 and Hormuz risk elevated.
events.what_to_watch: The next meeting on November 29 and whether geopolitics forces a policy response.

events.title: Iran-Qatar talks on two-day Hormuz reopening plan
events.why_it_matters: Iran has agreed to a Qatari-brokered plan to reopen Hormuz within two days if the US meets conditions, a potential de-escalation that could remove a large oil risk premium.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the US accepts the conditions and whether a draft deal is formalised.

top_risks: A contested or delayed US midterm result could trigger sharp risk-off moves across equities and rates.
A upside surprise in Friday's US payrolls or next week's CPI would harden December Fed hike expectations and pressure duration-sensitive sectors.
Iran-Hormuz talks could collapse, sending Brent back above $120 and reigniting global inflation fears.
Anthropic's IPO pricing below the $1.5-2tn target would be a major negative signal for AI sentiment and the broader tech complex.
The December 11 government funding deadline remains a tail risk for a partial shutdown, though it is outside the two-week window.
top_opportunities: A clean Democratic midterm sweep could unlock fiscal support and reduce trade-policy uncertainty, benefiting cyclicals and small caps.
A Hormuz reopening deal would be strongly bullish for airlines, transports, and consumer discretionary via lower energy costs.
Apple and AMD earnings could stabilise tech sentiment if results beat lowered expectations.
Anthropic's IPO, if well received, could revive the IPO market and boost AI-linked names.
A soft payrolls print would reduce December hike odds and support bonds and growth stocks.
summary: Markets enter the midterm election and a dense macro week with the Fed on hold but explicitly hawkish, inflation still sticky, and oil prices whipsawing on Hormuz diplomacy. The coming fortnight is dominated by the US midterms, payrolls, CPI, mega-cap tech earnings, and the RBA/BoE decisions, with Anthropic's blockbuster IPO as a sentiment wildcard. The main tension is between a market pricing a benign pause and a data-dependent path that could still force a December hike.
